title: Vectors — R's Core Data Structure
content: Vectors are R's fundamental type: `v <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)`. R is 1-indexed (not 0). Access: `v[1]` = first element. Slice: `v[2:4]`. Logical indexing: `v[v > 3]`. Vectorized operations: `v * 2`, `v + 10` apply element-wise. Named vectors: `named <- c(a=1, b=2); named["a"]`. `length(v)` = size. Coercion hierarchy: logical < integer < double < complex < character.

title: Data Frames
content: Create: `df <- data.frame(name=c("A","B"), score=c(90,85))`. View structure: `str(df)`. First rows: `head(df, 10)`. Dimensions: `dim(df)`. Column: `df$score` or `df[,"score"]`. Row filter: `df[df$score > 85, ]`. Add column: `df$grade <- ifelse(df$score >= 90, "A", "B")`. Remove column: `df$col <- NULL`. Rename: `colnames(df)[2] <- "marks"`.

title: Data Manipulation with dplyr
content: `filter()` rows: `filter(df, score > 80)`. `select()` cols: `select(df, name, score)`. `mutate()` add/modify: `mutate(df, grade = score/10)`. `arrange()` sort: `arrange(df, desc(score))`. `summarise()` aggregate: `summarise(df, avg=mean(score))`. `group_by()` + `summarise()`: `df %>% group_by(dept) %>% summarise(avg=mean(salary))`. Pipe `%>%` chains operations left-to-right.

title: Reshaping Data with tidyr
content: `pivot_longer()` converts wide → long format: `pivot_longer(df, cols=c(Q1,Q2), names_to="quarter", values_to="revenue")`. `pivot_wider()` converts long → wide. `separate()` splits one column into many: `separate(df, full_name, into=c("first","last"), sep=" ")`. `unite()` combines columns. `fill()` fills NA values from adjacent rows. `drop_na()` removes rows with any NA.

title: Data Visualization with ggplot2
content: ggplot2 uses grammar of graphics: `ggplot(data, aes(x,y)) + geom_*()`. Scatter: `geom_point()`. Line: `geom_line()`. Bar: `geom_bar(stat="identity")`. Histogram: `geom_histogram(bins=30)`. Color by group: `aes(color=category)`. Facet (subplots): `facet_wrap(~group)`. Labels: `labs(title="T", x="X", y="Y")`. Theme: `theme_minimal()`. Save: `ggsave("plot.png", width=8, height=5)`.

title: Handling NA & NULL in R
content: NA = missing value; NULL = empty object. Detect: `is.na(x)`. Count NAs: `sum(is.na(df$col))`. Remove rows with any NA: `na.omit(df)` or `df[complete.cases(df),]`. Compute ignoring NA: `mean(x, na.rm=TRUE)`. Replace NA: `df$col[is.na(df$col)] <- 0`. With dplyr: `mutate(df, col=replace_na(col, 0))`. With tidyr: `replace_na(list(col=0))`.

title: Apply Family & Functional Programming
content: `apply(matrix, 1, fn)` applies fn to each row (1) or column (2). `lapply(list, fn)` returns a list. `sapply(list, fn)` simplifies to vector/matrix if possible. `tapply(data, group, fn)` applies fn per group. `vapply(list, fn, type)` is safer sapply with expected type. Modern alternative: `purrr::map(list, fn)` returns list, `map_dbl` for doubles. Avoid explicit for-loops when these suffice.

title: Functions in R
content: Define: `add <- function(a, b=0) { a + b }`. Last expression is returned (no explicit `return` needed). Call by name: `add(b=3, a=1)`. Variable args: `function(...){ args <- list(...) }`. Scoping: R uses lexical scoping — functions search the environment where they were defined. Closures: `make_adder <- function(n) function(x) x+n`. Anonymous: `(function(x) x^2)(5)`.

title: String Manipulation
content: Concatenate: `paste("Hello", "World")` or `paste0("no","space")`. `sprintf("%s scored %.1f%%", name, score)`. Length: `nchar(s)`. Substring: `substr(s, 1, 5)`. Pattern match: `grepl(pattern, s)`. Replace: `gsub(pattern, replacement, s)`. Split: `strsplit(s, ",")[[1]]`. With stringr: `str_trim()`, `str_pad()`, `str_detect()`, `str_replace_all()`, `str_split_fixed()`.

title: Lists in R
content: Lists are heterogeneous containers: `lst <- list(name="Alice", scores=c(90,85), active=TRUE)`. Access by name: `lst$name` or `lst[["name"]]`. By position: `lst[[2]]`. Single `[` returns a list (subset), double `[[` returns the element. Modify: `lst$age <- 25`. Nested: `lst$address$city`. Convert to vector: `unlist(lst)`. Use lists for JSON-like structures and return values from functions.

title: Control Flow in R
content: `if (cond) { ... } else if (cond2) { ... } else { ... }`. Vectorized: `ifelse(cond_vec, yes_vec, no_vec)`. For loop: `for (i in 1:10) { ... }`. While: `while (cond) { ... }`. `break` exits loop; `next` skips to next iteration. `repeat { ... if(done) break }`. In R, prefer vectorized operations and `apply` family over explicit loops for performance.

title: Descriptive Statistics
content: `mean(x)`, `median(x)`, `sd(x)` (std dev), `var(x)`. Range: `range(x)` → min & max. Quantiles: `quantile(x, probs=c(0.25,0.75))`. Summary: `summary(df)` gives min/Q1/median/mean/Q3/max per column. Correlation: `cor(x, y)` or `cor(df)` for matrix. Frequency table: `table(df$category)`. Test normality: `shapiro.test(x)`.

title: Joining Data Frames
content: Base R: `merge(x, y, by="id")` (inner join by default). Left join: `merge(x, y, all.x=TRUE)`. Full join: `merge(x, y, all=TRUE)`. dplyr (preferred): `inner_join(x, y, by="id")`, `left_join()`, `right_join()`, `full_join()`, `anti_join()` (rows in x not in y). Join on different col names: `by=c("x_col"="y_col")`. Multiple keys: `by=c("id","date")`.

title: Reading & Writing Data
content: CSV: `df <- read.csv("file.csv")` or faster `readr::read_csv("file.csv")`. Write: `write.csv(df, "out.csv", row.names=FALSE)`. Excel: `readxl::read_excel("file.xlsx", sheet=1)`. RDS (R binary): `saveRDS(obj, "file.rds"); obj <- readRDS("file.rds")`. JSON: `jsonlite::fromJSON("file.json")`. Specify encoding: `read.csv("file.csv", fileEncoding="UTF-8")`.

title: Environments & Scoping
content: R has a search path of environments. `globalenv()` is your workspace. `baseenv()` has base functions. `new.env()` creates an isolated environment. Assign into env: `assign("x", 10, envir=myenv)`. Get: `get("x", envir=myenv)`. `<<-` assigns to parent scope (use with caution). `environment(fn)` returns where fn was defined. Environments are first-class — used for namespaces, closures, and R5/R6 classes.
